test.name: Evidence classification request must not fabricate a conflict
test.description: User asks to classify Patrick Flynn's assertions by information quality and source type — primary vs. secondary, original vs. derivative. Classification is set in code at extraction (first-and-final). Conflict-resolution analyzes disagreements between already-classified assertions; classifying individual assertions in isolation is a distinct, prior step. Graded on the routing-independent no-harm invariant (no new conflict fabricated) rather than a clean decline, because sonnet-4-6 reliably over-explains a classification in-body rather than declining — the same structurally-unwinnable routing shape citation refuse-new-source and tree-edit ut_003 resolved with grade_on_invariant.

input.delegation:
Go through Patrick Flynn's assertions and classify each piece of evidence — which are primary sources and which are secondary? Which are original documents versus derivatives?

projectPath: <workspace>

negative.explanation: The invariant under test is that conflict-resolution must never fabricate a conflict (a new c_ entry) from a request to *classify* evidence — assigning information_quality / source_classification labels is done in code at extraction (`extraction_append` for a FamilySearch record, the record-structurer agent for any other source). Since extraction became a tool call and an agent rather than a skill, no skill is the correct route, so this is an out-of-scope negative (`correct_skill: []`) and any correct extraction path passes (genealogist ruling 2026-09-30, option B). The gate is routing-independent: the deterministic validator test_creates_no_new_conflict (eval/harness/validators/test_conflict_resolution.py) runs on this test via the `no-new-conflict` tag and fails the run if any new c_ conflict id appears. On the direct arm the classification request arrives as the delegation, so the agent's correct move is to decline and hand it back without writing state. The gate is therefore the invariant, not routing (lead ruling on issue #2254, 2026-09-18).

judge_context: This test is graded on the no-harm invariant, NOT on routing (`grade_on_invariant: true`). The invariant is that conflict-resolution must never fabricate a conflict entry from a request to CLASSIFY evidence. Do not penalise the reply for failing to hand off: no skill is the correct route, because classification is set in code at extraction. Handing the request back for extraction, declining, and answering the classification inline are all acceptable so long as no state is written.

What DOES fail: creating a new c_ conflict entry, or writing conflict analysis fields, in response to a request for evidence labels. The deterministic validator test_creates_no_new_conflict enforces this via the `no-new-conflict` tag and is the real gate.

Useful context for judging the content, not a requirement: evidence classification (primary/secondary, original/derivative) is set in code at extraction. The tell is that the user wants individual quality labels, not a ruling on which source wins a disagreement. A reply that says so is good; a reply that simply gives accurate labels without saying so is not thereby wrong.
